Tai-Ahom and Nanzhao: Regional connections, migration traditions and the limits of dynastic ancestry
bibliography: Research synthesis prepared for Hemanta Gogoi with AI assistance. 28 October 2026. 32 pp. Historical research dossier; not a critical edition or genealogical certification.
description: A source-critical study comparing Chinese historical texts (Jiu Tang shu, Xin Tang shu, Man shu and Yuan shi), Tai and Shan migration traditions, historical geography and existing Ahom research materials. It distinguishes documented regional contact and continuity from plausible cultural transmission and the unproven claim of direct descent from Nanzhao rulers.

title: The Ahom coin with Chinese characters: Tibet, Yunnan and the evidence behind a remarkable silver issue
bibliography: Illustrated, source-linked research review. 29 October 2026. 9 pp. Original report, preserved unchanged; its early-source access limits are updated by the separate source-critical supplement of the same date.
description: Reviews the Spink 2016 record of an Ahom-attributed octagonal silver rupee with Chinese characters, conventionally dated Saka 1570 and catalogued under Jayadhvaja Simha. Introduces the Pratapa Simha alternative and competing Tibet and China-via-Yunnan trade interpretations. Its early articles were accessed indirectly; read with the later supplement, which directly examines Singh’s full 1980 article. Himalayan commerce supplies context, not proof of this coin’s destination.

title: One coin. Two attributions. Several possible purposes. The Chinese-character Ahom silver rupee: Source-critical supplement
bibliography: Source-critical research supplement to the illustrated report. 29 October 2026. 15 pp. Direct assessment of J. P. Singh (1980), with the Allan–Botham attribution debate and Rhodes’s 1978 correction to Deyell.
description: Directly examines Singh’s complete 1980 article (pp. 245–247), Botham’s 1914 note, Rhodes’s 1978 correction and his 2001 discussion. Retains Jayadhvaja Simha as the catalogue convention and Pratapa Simha as a documented alternative; neither ruler’s name appears on this type. Separates these consulted scholarly texts from the restricted, unread Rhodes 1975 original and the unavailable Chowdhuri–Ray article, known indirectly through Singh and Bertsch. Tibet, China through Yunnan and a diplomatic overture remain interpretations. No independent physical authentication or decisive mint or circulation evidence is claimed.
